summary: This bill amends Title IX to define 'sex' as an individual's biologically determined sex as male or female, with 'female' and 'male' defined by their reproductive systems that produce ova or sperm.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends Title IX definitions for sex-based nondiscrimination in federally funded education programs. It contains no provisions altering appropriations, budgets, or federal expenditures.
No provisions address tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue collection.
The bill is confined to education programs under Title IX and does not regulate healthcare delivery, insurance, or medical policy.
No connection to firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions related to immigration, visas, borders, or enforcement.
While the bill defines sex via reproductive biology and gametes, it does not address abortion access, restrictions, or reproductive rights policy.
No provisions on military funding, defense policy, or armed forces.
No environmental, regulatory, or climate-related content.
No provisions affecting welfare programs, food assistance, or entitlement spending.

The bill directly amends Title IX nondiscrimination rules for education programs receiving federal funds by codifying a biological definition of sex. However, it does not address school funding levels, federal involvement in curriculum, school choice, or privatization.
No provisions on drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.
No provisions on sentencing, policing, rehabilitation, or criminal procedure.
No provisions on tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
No provisions addressing deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.

The bill explicitly redefines 'sex' under Title IX as biologically determined (male/female based on gamete production) and excludes gender identity. This directly limits the scope of protections available to transgender individuals in education programs, pushing strongly toward restricting LGBTQ+ legal protections in this domain.
No provisions on foreign assistance or international aid.
No provisions on voting access, election integrity, or electoral procedures.
No provisions on technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
No provisions on worker protections, collective bargaining, or union rights.

The bill strengthens biological-sex nondiscrimination rules under Title IX but does not address religious exemptions, conscience protections, or conflicts between civil rights enforcement and religious liberty.
